description: Event-handler silent-drop surveillance. Each panel surfaces a fire-and-forget path that swallows errors at runtime, so a non-zero rate means data is being dropped without raising. Rows group the drops by what is lost: a queued job, an audit-trail entry, a federated projection, a SIEM record, or a config reload.

panels.description: At-a-glance summary across every silent-drop counter on this dashboard, which is now every drop-class counter the engine registers except the ones that fail loudly elsewhere (webhook and federation DLQs, pool and rate-limit degradation). Non-zero means something is being dropped on the floor right now. Every term carries `or vector(0)` because most of these counters are labelled, a labelled counter has no series until its first increment, and sum() over no series is an empty vector: without the guard one never-incremented counter made the whole sum empty and this tile read "No data" while the others climbed. A coverage test in the API build fails if a new drop counter is added without a panel here or a documented reason it does not belong, and if any term in a multi-counter sum loses its guard.

panels.title: Silent drops — total events dropped in last 24h

panels.description: Cascade-cancel enqueue failures — when a parent record terminalizes, children are supposed to fan out and cancel. A failure here orphans a child that may keep executing. Highest operational stakes on this dashboard.
panels.title: Cascade-cancel enqueue failures (drops/sec) — agledger_cascade_cancel_enqueue_failures_total

panels.description: Webhook dispatch-time enqueue failures. Distinct from `agledger_webhooks_failed_total` which is the *delivery* failure counter — this is the one-step-earlier failure where the webhook never made it onto the queue at all. Customer never sees it; we never retry it.
panels.title: Webhook enqueue failures (drops/sec) — agledger_webhook_enqueue_failures_total

panels.description: Cascading-verification enqueue failures. The recovery sweep is the safety net for stuck records, but this counter measures dispatch-time drops — the rate at which we lean on the sweep to catch up.
panels.title: Cascading-gate enqueue failures

panels.description: Phase-2 gate enqueue failures. Same sweep-safety-net pattern as cascading-gate — non-zero rate means we're papering over a queue or DB issue with the periodic sweep.
panels.title: Phase-2 enqueue failures

panels.description: Federation outbound enqueue failures. State-transitions or signals that didn't make it onto the federation outbound queue. The peer never sees them; the chain on the peer's side stays out of sync.
panels.title: Federation outbound enqueue failures

panels.description: Bus-handler enqueue failures in the federation outbound publisher. The record transitioned locally and no outbound job exists, so the peer never learns of it.
panels.title: Federation outbound publish enqueue failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: Inline Phase 2 gate evaluation threw inside submitCompletion. pg-boss and the recovery sweep are the safety nets, so this measures how often the fast path is falling back rather than data loss on its own.
panels.title: Inline Phase-2 gate failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: A cascade-rollup job gave up after every pg-boss retry. If the failing job was the last child's, the parent is stranded ACTIVE with every child terminal and nothing rolls it up; if other children were still outstanding, a later one rolls the parent up normally and only this attempt was lost. The auto-rollup consistency sweep (agledger_auto_rollup_stuck_parents_total, data-integrity dashboard) is what distinguishes the two. That sweep runs every five minutes and only counts a parent idle for five, so expect it five to ten minutes later. This counter names the cause at the moment it happens.
panels.title: Cascade-rollup retries exhausted (drops/sec)

panels.description: A principal-mode advisory gate pass crashed through every retry. Nothing terminalizes wrongly (the record correctly keeps awaiting its principal verdict), but the advisory annotation the customer expected on it is gone for good. A sustained rate means the engine is systematically failing on one contract type.
panels.title: Advisory gate passes lost (drops/sec)

panels.description: Auth-audit persistence failures. Login/logout/key-use audit rows that didn't make it into system_audit_log. SIEM polls that table — drops here are gaps in the customer's compliance feed.
panels.title: Auth-audit persistence failures — agledger_auth_audit_persist_failures_total

panels.description: Reputation cache update failures. Intentionally swallowed at the call site (reputation is eventual-consistency convenience, not chain data) — this counter measures the eventual-consistency drift rate.
panels.title: Reputation cache update failures

panels.description: Persist-event failed INSIDE the cascading-gate enqueue-failure recovery handler. The outer counter ticked too: this is the audit trail going missing when both layers fail.
panels.title: Cascading-gate recovery persist-event failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: Same shape as the cascading-gate pair: persist-event failed inside the Phase 2 enqueue-failure recovery handler, so the failure itself left no /v1/events row.
panels.title: Phase-2 recovery persist-event failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: A withTransaction post-commit callback threw AFTER the commit succeeded. Usually a lost bus emit or webhook fan-out: the state change is durable and the notification of it is gone.
panels.title: Post-commit callback failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: Support-bundle vault audit-log writes dropped. The bundle was produced and the record that it was produced is missing.
panels.title: Support-bundle audit writes dropped (drops/sec)

panels.description: Fire-and-forget audit_vault appends from federation outbound that failed and were swallowed: the chain entry never landed. Highest stakes on this dashboard alongside cascade-cancel, because the chain is the product.
panels.title: Federation audit-vault appends dropped (drops/sec)

panels.description: Fire-and-forget record_federation_state writes that failed and were swallowed. The Server believes a peer is in a state it was never told about.
panels.title: Federation record-state writes dropped (drops/sec)

panels.description: Forensic/schema audit writes on the federation REJECT path that were swallowed, so a rejected peer attempt or digest mismatch left no forensic trail. The rejection was correct and unprovable.
panels.title: Federation forensic-audit writes dropped (drops/sec)

panels.description: Sender-side persistEvent calls in the outbound publisher that failed and were swallowed: /v1/events is missing federation.* rows this Server did emit.
panels.title: Federation outbound persist-event dropped (drops/sec)

panels.description: SIEM OCSF mapper failures by event_type. When a mapper throws, the event never reaches the file or HTTP sender — it's dropped before the SIEM sees it. Non-zero by event_type tells you which mapping is broken.
panels.title: SIEM mapper failures

panels.description: SIEM HTTP batches dropped after delivery failure. BUS EVENTS ONLY: polled system_audit_log rows no longer pass through this sender's buffer, and a batch a collector refuses on that path is retried from an unadvanced cursor rather than dropped. So 0 here does NOT mean the compliance feed is complete. For the polled path read SIEM poll deliveries refused alongside it.
panels.title: SIEM HTTP batches dropped

panels.description: SIEM file lines dropped: a failed write, a line written after close, or the buffer capped while the stream was backed up. File-mode SIEM is missing those lines. A stalled disk now drops and counts here instead of growing the heap without bound, so this can move on a slow disk that used to look silent.
panels.title: SIEM file lines dropped

panels.description: A system_audit_log poll cycle threw (query or cursor-persist). The poller retries from the unadvanced cursor, so this is recoverable, but a sustained rate means the SIEM feed is stalled.
panels.title: SIEM poll-cycle failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: A configured sink refused a polled batch, so the cursor did not advance and the next cycle re-reads the same rows. NOT a drop: nothing is lost and the backlog drains when the sink returns. This is the metric that separates a delivery stall from a watermark stall when agledger_siem_poll_lag_seconds climbs, and it is the first thing AGLedgerSiemPollerFallingBehind tells you to check. Labelled by sink.
panels.title: SIEM poll deliveries refused

panels.description: A cross-replica cache-invalidation event was dropped. Replicas serve stale schemas until the next TTL expiry.
panels.title: Cache-invalidation events dropped (drops/sec)

panels.description: Async warmCache re-warm failed off a cross-replica schema invalidation. Degrades to the name-resolved entry rather than losing data, but a publisher-scoped hint is gone until the next refresh.
panels.title: Schema warm-cache refresh failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: Provisioning hot-reload failed. The running config no longer matches the YAML the operator edited, and nothing else says so.
panels.title: Provisioning hot-reload failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: An llms.txt override/prepend/append file failed to load, and the built-in template was served instead. Catches a typo in AGLEDGER_LLMS_TXT_*_PATH that is otherwise invisible: the endpoint keeps returning 200.
panels.title: llms.txt customization load failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: Debounced api_keys.last_used_at UPDATE failures. Key rotation reviews read last_used_at to decide what is dormant, so a sustained rate makes an active key look unused.
panels.title: api_keys.last_used_at update failures (drops/sec)

panels.description: Webhook subscription lifecycle changes (create, update, URL repoint, delete, secret rotation, pause, resume) whose audit row could not be persisted. The write is fire-and-forget by design, because the mutation has already committed and a failed audit must not fail the caller, so this counter is the only thing that reports a lost egress-config record. A URL repoint that lands here is an egress channel redirected with no trace.
panels.title: Webhook lifecycle audit drops
